description: Positive and negative numbers and their operations

lessons.title: Positive and Negative
lessons.intro: Integers include zero, the counting numbers, AND their negatives — numbers below zero.
explanation: Zero is an integer too, neither positive nor negative.
We use negatives for things like temperature below zero or debt.
lessons.rule: Integers are positive numbers, negatives and zero.
lessons.tip: The '-' sign shows a number below zero.

steps.text: Each positive has an opposite negative.
steps.tip: Opposites are the same distance from 0.

lessons.title: Opposites
lessons.intro: Every integer has an opposite — the same distance from zero but the other side.
lessons.rule: An integer's opposite has the same size, other sign.
lessons.tip: Opposites always add to zero.

lessons.title: Comparing Negatives
lessons.intro: With negatives, bigger-looking numbers can actually be smaller!
explanation: -2 is greater than -5 (it is closer to zero).
On a number line, right is always greater.
The more negative a number, the smaller it is.
lessons.rule: The number further right on the line is greater.
lessons.tip: -1 is greater than -100.

lessons.title: Integers in Real Life
lessons.intro: Negatives describe real situations: cold temperatures, depths, and debts.
explanation: A profit is positive; a loss is negative.
lessons.rule: Below zero, below sea level and debt are negatives.
lessons.tip: Above/gain is positive; below/loss is negative.

lessons.title: Ordering Integers
lessons.intro: We can line up integers from smallest to largest on the number line.
explanation: Negatives come first, then zero, then positives.
The smallest is the most negative.
lessons.rule: Smallest = most negative; largest = most positive.
lessons.tip: Place them on a line to be sure.

quiz.question: What is the opposite of +5?
What is the opposite of -3?
Which is greater, -2 or -5? Write the greater one.
Write 'three degrees below zero' as an integer.
A submarine is 20 metres below sea level. Write its position as an integer.
A shopkeeper makes a profit of 50 rupees. Write this as an integer.
quiz.story: A good day at the shop.

quiz.question: From the list -3, 0, 2, -1, write the smallest number.
Which is greater, -10 or -1? Write the greater one.

lessons.title: The Integer Number Line
lessons.intro: The number line stretches both ways from zero: positives right, negatives left.
explanation: Moving right adds; moving left subtracts.
lessons.rule: Right is positive, left is negative on the line.
lessons.tip: Zero is the middle of the integer line.

lessons.title: Moving on the Line
lessons.intro: To add, move right; to subtract, move left.
explanation: Start at 2, move 5 left: land on -3.
Start at -1, move 3 right: land on 2.
Count the steps carefully, watching direction.
lessons.rule: Add = move right; subtract = move left.
lessons.tip: Begin at the first number, then step.

lessons.title: Lifts and Floors
lessons.intro: A building with basements is a perfect integer number line.
explanation: Floor -2 going up 5 floors reaches floor 3.
Going up adds, going down subtracts.
lessons.rule: Up adds, down subtracts — just like the line.
lessons.tip: Floor 0 is the ground floor.

lessons.title: Distance on the Line
lessons.intro: The distance between two integers is how many steps apart they are — always positive.
explanation: Count from one to the other.
Distance ignores direction, so it is never negative.
lessons.rule: Distance = steps between numbers (always positive).
lessons.tip: Add the two distances from zero if signs differ.

lessons.title: Midpoints
lessons.intro: The midpoint of two integers is exactly halfway between them.
explanation: Add the two numbers and halve.
The midpoint is equally far from both ends.
lessons.rule: Midpoint = (first + second) / 2.
lessons.tip: Check it is the same distance from each end.

quiz.question: On a number line, what number is 3 steps right of 0?
What number is 4 steps left of 0?
Start at 2 and move 5 steps left. Where do you land?
Start at -1 and move 3 steps right. Where do you land?
A lift at floor -2 goes up 5 floors. Which floor does it reach?
The temperature is -5 degrees and rises by 8 degrees. What is the new temperature?
What is the distance between -3 and 4 on the number line?
What integer is exactly halfway between -6 and 2?

lessons.title: Adding Integers
lessons.intro: Adding a positive moves right; adding a negative moves left.
explanation: Same signs add, different signs find the difference.
lessons.rule: Add positives by moving right, negatives by moving left.
lessons.tip: Different signs: subtract and keep the bigger sign.

lessons.title: Same Signs
lessons.intro: When both integers have the same sign, add their sizes and keep the sign.
explanation: Same signs make the result bigger in size.
lessons.rule: Same signs: add sizes, keep the shared sign.
lessons.tip: Two negatives make a bigger negative.

lessons.title: Different Signs
lessons.intro: With different signs, subtract the smaller size from the bigger and keep the bigger sign.
lessons.rule: Different signs: subtract, keep the bigger number's sign.
lessons.tip: Equal opposites give zero.

lessons.title: Adding and Money
lessons.intro: Earning is positive, owing is negative — adding them gives your balance.
explanation: Add earnings and debts to find the net.
lessons.rule: Net balance = earnings (+) plus debts (-).
lessons.tip: A negative total means you still owe.

lessons.title: Adding Three Integers
lessons.intro: Add integers one at a time, keeping track of the running total.
explanation: Grouping positives and negatives first can help.
lessons.rule: Add step by step, left to right.
lessons.tip: You can add all positives, then all negatives.

quiz.question: What is -3 + 5?
What is 4 + (-6)?
What is -7 + (-2)?
What is -5 + 5?
The temperature is -4 degrees and rises by 10 degrees. What is the new temperature?
Sara owes 8 rupees and then earns 3 rupees. What is her balance as an integer (negative means she owes)?
quiz.hint: Owe is negative, earn is positive.

quiz.question: What is -12 + 7 + 3?

lessons.title: Subtracting Integers
lessons.intro: Subtracting an integer is the same as adding its opposite — a powerful rule!
lessons.rule: To subtract, add the opposite: a - b = a + (-b).
lessons.tip: Two minuses in a row make a plus.

steps.text: Rewrite subtraction as adding the opposite.

lessons.title: Going Below Zero
lessons.intro: Subtracting a bigger number takes you below zero.
explanation: The result is negative when you subtract more than you have.
Move left past zero on the line.
lessons.rule: Subtracting more than you have gives a negative.
lessons.tip: Count the steps past zero.

lessons.title: Minus a Negative
lessons.intro: Subtracting a negative is like adding — the two signs make a plus.
lessons.rule: Subtracting a negative adds a positive.
lessons.tip: Replace '--' with '+' first.

lessons.title: Temperature Drops
lessons.intro: Falling temperatures are a natural subtraction of integers.
explanation: Below zero shows as a negative temperature.
lessons.rule: A drop subtracts; below zero is negative.
lessons.tip: Start high, step down.

lessons.title: Subtraction Master
lessons.intro: With the 'add the opposite' rule, any integer subtraction is easy.
lessons.rule: Rewrite every subtraction as an addition, then solve.
lessons.tip: The opposite flips the sign.

quiz.question: What is 5 - 8?
What is -3 - 4?
What is 2 - (-3)?
What is -5 - (-2)?
The temperature is 3 degrees and falls by 7 degrees. What is the new temperature?
From floor -1, a lift goes down 4 floors. Which floor does it reach?
What is -6 - (-10)?
What is 0 - (-7)?

lessons.title: Multiplying Integers
lessons.intro: The sign rule for multiplication: same signs give positive, different signs give negative.
explanation: Multiply the sizes, then decide the sign.
lessons.rule: Same signs -> positive; different signs -> negative.
lessons.tip: Count the minus signs: even = +, odd = -.

lessons.title: Dividing Integers
lessons.intro: Division follows the SAME sign rule as multiplication.
explanation: Divide the sizes, then apply the sign rule.
lessons.rule: Division sign rule matches multiplication.
lessons.tip: Same signs positive, different signs negative.

lessons.title: Repeated Steps
lessons.intro: Multiplying models repeated movement, like a diver descending each minute.
explanation: Descending 3 m each minute for 4 minutes: (-3) x 4 = -12.
Repeated loss is multiplication by a negative.
lessons.rule: Repeated equal change = multiplication.
lessons.tip: Loss each step gives a negative product.

lessons.title: Counting the Minus Signs
lessons.intro: When several negatives multiply, count them: even minuses give positive, odd give negative.
explanation: Count signs before you compute the size.
lessons.rule: Even number of minus signs -> positive result.
lessons.tip: Odd number of minuses -> negative result.

lessons.title: Integer Master
lessons.intro: Combine add, subtract, multiply and divide with full sign confidence.
explanation: Work left to right, tracking signs.
A quick sign check prevents mistakes.
lessons.rule: Track signs carefully through every step.
lessons.tip: Do the arithmetic, then confirm the sign.

quiz.question: What is (-3) x 4?
What is (-2) x (-5)?
What is (-12) / 3?
A diver descends 3 metres each minute for 4 minutes. What is her depth as an integer?
The temperature falls 2 degrees each hour for 5 hours. What is the total change as an integer?
quiz.hint: A fall each hour is negative.
